chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:
I sent a message to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that a woman's mother had been an umm walad, then she died, and the woman wanted to perform hajj on her behalf.
He said, “Did she not become free through her child? She may perform hajj on her behalf.”

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: a slave-concubine who bore her master a child

ai.seo_question: Can hajj be performed on behalf of a deceased umm walad who became free through her child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning performing hajj on behalf of a deceased umm walad. The Imam عليه السلام indicates that since she had attained freedom through her child, hajj may be performed on her behalf after her death.
